DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 1, OPENING

# Opening: Jesus had no human biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed begot the child. My thesis is that the KJV text gives Jesus a mother, Mary, and a conception by the Holy Ghost. It gives him no man who begot him. Joseph was the husband of Mary and the one who named the child, but he was not the one who begot him.

## 1. The conception is "of the Holy Ghost," and it happened before Mary and Joseph came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Prin ē synelthein autous* (πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν αὐτούς) means "before they came together." *Synerchomai* (G4905) means to come together as a married couple. *Ek pneumatos hagiou* (ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου) means "out of the Holy Spirit." The preposition *ek* (G1537) marks the source. The text therefore places the pregnancy before any union with Joseph and names its source as the Holy Ghost.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** *Gennēthen* (γεννηθέν, from G1080 *gennaō*) means "begotten" or "conceived." In the same verse it is again paired with *ek pneumatos* (out of the Spirit). The angel gives the source of the begetting to Joseph in order to settle whether Joseph was the source.

**[L3]** Compare Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily." If Joseph had begotten the child, there would have been nothing to resolve and no reason to put her away. The angel's words in 1:20 answer his doubt by naming a different source.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 puts the pregnancy before the coming together [L1, L2]. Matthew 1:19 shows that Joseph was troubled by it [L3]. Matthew 1:20 gives the Holy Ghost as the *ek* (source) [L2]. So the text excludes Joseph as the begetter.

## 2. Mary had not known a man, and Joseph "knew her not" until the birth

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** *Andra ou ginōskō* (ἄνδρα οὐ γινώσκω) means "I do not know a man." *Ginōskō* (G1097) is used here of marital knowledge. The present tense states her standing at the time of the announcement.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain." The Hebrew *yada* (H3045), to know, is the same idiom, and in that verse conception follows the knowing. Luke 1:34 uses the idiom in the negative, so no conception by man follows.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son: and he called his name JESUS."

**[L2]** *Ouk eginōsken* (οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν) means "he was not knowing her." *Heōs hou* (ἕως οὗ) means "until which time." The imperfect tense marks continued abstinence through the whole period up to the birth.

**[L4]** Mary says she has not known a man [L1 Luke 1:34, L2 *ginōskō*]. The idiom for fathering is the same one used for Adam and Eve [L3 Genesis 4:1]. Joseph did not know her until the birth [L1 Matthew 1:25, L2 imperfect]. Therefore no man's seed was involved in the conception.

## 3. The angel states the mechanism and ties the child's title to it

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** *Epeleusetai* (ἐπελεύσεται) means "shall come upon." *Episkiasei* (ἐπισκιάσει) means "shall overshadow." *Dio kai* (διὸ καί) means "for which reason also," so the title rests on the conception. *Gennōmenon* (γεννώμενον) means "that which is being begotten." The child is "of thee" (*ek sou*), from Mary alone.

**[L3]** Luke 1:27 gives Mary's status: "to a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph... and the virgin's name was Mary." The word is *parthenos* (G3933), virgin, at the point of the announcement.

**[L4]** The Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest are the named agents [L1, L2]. The child is "of thee," from Mary [L2]. The title "Son of God" is grounded in this by *dio kai* [L2]. The announcement is made to a *parthenos* [L3]. So the begetting was a miraculous act of God and not a union with a man.

## 4. Joseph is "husband" and "supposed" father, never the one who begat

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The genealogy before this verse uses *egennēsen* (ἐγέννησεν), "begat," in the active voice for each father in turn. At the end the pattern changes. Joseph is *ton andra Marias* (τὸν ἄνδρα Μαρίας), "the husband of Mary." The next verb is the passive *egennēthē* (ἐγεννήθη), "was born." The relative pronoun is *hēs* (ἧς), "of whom," in the feminine singular. Its only feminine antecedent is Mary, so Jesus is said to be born of her.

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."

**[L2]** *Hōs enomizeto* (ὡς ἐνομίζετο) means "as was reckoned" or "as was supposed." *Nomizō* (G3543) is used of what is thought or assumed. Luke's wording marks the common opinion as differing from the fact.

**[L3]** Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled." The KJV gives the name Joseph here. Luke 2:49 supplies the child's own answer to Mary's "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing" (Luke 2:48): "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" The child corrects the term "father."

**[L4]** The genealogy breaks its "begat" pattern at Joseph [L1, L2]. Luke records that the opinion was only "supposed" [L1, L2]. Luke 2:49 shows the child himself answering Mary's "thy father" with "my father's business" [L3]. So the references to Joseph as father are about legal standing and what people supposed.

## 5. Prophecy and the apostle's wording name only a woman

**[L1]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L2]** *Almah* (H5959) is the word for virgin. The same verse says it will be an *'oth* (H226), a sign, which would be no sign if it were an ordinary conception.

**[L3]** Genesis 24:43 uses *almah* of Rebekah, and Genesis 24:16 describes her: "a virgin, neither had any man known her." Matthew 1:22-23 quotes the prophecy as fulfilled and renders *almah* as *parthenos* (G3933): "Behold, a virgin shall be with child."

**[L1]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law."

**[L2]** *Genomenon ek gynaikos* (γενόμενον ἐκ γυναικός) means "come to be out of a woman." Only the woman is named as the source.

**[L4]** Isaiah's *almah* is a sign [L2]. It is the same word applied to a woman "neither had any man known her" [L3 Genesis 24:16, 24:43]. Matthew reads it as *parthenos* [L3 Matthew 1:22-23]. Paul names only the woman [L1, L2]. So the prophecy and the apostle's wording fit a conception without a human father.

## 6. Anticipated objections

- **"His parents" (Luke 2:41) and "thy father" (Luke 2:48).** **[L1]** Luke 2:41: "Now his parents went to Jerusalem every year." **[L2]** *Goneis* (G1118) means "parents" and covers legal guardians, so it does not state who begat. **[L3]** Luke 2:49 answers Luke 2:48: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" **[L4]** Luke 3:23, which says "as was supposed" [L1, L2], gives the reading for such terms.
- **"Seed of David" (Romans 1:3).** The descent from David runs through Mary's line and through Joseph's legal standing. Matthew 1:16 names Mary as the one of whom Jesus was born [L1, L2].

## DECLARED CHAIN -- the links your case stands on:

1. The conception was out of the Holy Ghost before Mary and Joseph came together. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:18, 1:20; [L2] *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit), *prin ē synelthein* (before coming together), *gennēthen* (begotten); [L3] Matthew 1:19, Joseph's intent to put her away.
2. Mary had not known a man, and Joseph did not know her until after the birth. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25; [L2] *ginōskō* (to know), *ouk eginōsken* (was not knowing, imperfect), *heōs hou* (until which time); [L3] Genesis 4:1, *yada* (to know) leads to conception.
3. The Holy Ghost coming upon her and the power of the Highest overshadowing her is the stated mechanism, and "Son of God" is grounded in it. Footing: [L1] Luke 1:35; [L2] *epeleusetai* (shall come upon), *episkiasei* (shall overshadow), *dio kai* (for which reason also); [L3] Luke 1:27, *parthenos* (virgin).
4. Joseph is the husband and the supposed father, not the begetter. Footing: [L1] Matthew 1:16, Luke 3:23; [L2] *andra* (husband), *hēs* (of whom, feminine singular), *egennēthē* (was born, passive), *enomizeto* (was supposed); [L3] Luke 2:48-49, the child's answer "my father's business".
5. Isaiah's sign and Paul's wording name only a woman as the source. Footing: [L1] Isaiah 7:14, Galatians 4:4; [L2] *almah* (virgin), *'oth* (sign), *ek gynaikos* (out of a woman); [L3] Genesis 24:16, 24:43, Matthew 1:22-23.
6. Jesus had no human biological father; his conception was by the Holy Ghost from Mary alone, and Joseph was his husband-guardian and not his begetter. Footing: [L4] from links 1-5, resting on [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35 and [L2] *gennēthen* (begotten) with *ek pneumatos hagiou* (out of the Holy Spirit).

# Challenge: the seed is David's by the flesh, and the father the text names is Joseph

The defender's thesis is that "the KJV text gives Jesus a mother, Mary, and a conception by the Holy Ghost. It gives him no man who begot him." I answer from the rows the defender passed over. The promise to David requires a seed out of a man's loins. The text names one man as the child's father, Joseph, of the house of David. The defender's timing rows, read in their own order, bound the abstinence to the pregnancy. They do not cover the conception. I aim at the keystone **D6** and at the links it stands on.

---

## My chain, footed

**C1. The promise requires a seed out of a man's body, according to the flesh.**
- [L1] 2 Samuel 7:12: "I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom."
- [L2] *zera'* (H2233), seed, posterity. *me'im* (H4578), bowels, the inward parts of the body.
- [L3] Psalm 132:11: "Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne." The margin reads "Heb. belly," *beten* (H990).
- [L3] Acts 2:30: "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne." Here *osphys* (G3751) means loins, procreative power, and *kata sarka* means according to the flesh.
- [L3] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." The Greek is *ek spermatos* (G4690), out of seed.
- [L3] Hebrews 7:10 uses the same loins-word of a father: "For he was yet in the loins of his father."

[L4] The prophet's promise [L1, L2] and the apostles' applications [L3] place the seed in a man's loins and bowels, and they say it twice "according to the flesh." So the flesh of Christ came out of a Davidic man's loins.

**C2. The tribe is reckoned by the father's house, and the reckoning of Christ is "evident."**
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L3] Numbers 1:2: "after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L2] *le-veit avotam* means "by the house of their fathers." It is built on *bayith* (H1004), house, and *'ab* (H1), father.
- [L3] Ezra 2:62 records priests "called after the name" of a wife's house (Ezra 2:61): "therefore were they, as polluted, put from the priesthood."

[L4] The law counts a man's tribe by his father's house [L3, L2]. A register drawn through a wife's house was put away [L3]. So the "evident" descent from Judah [L1] runs through a father of Judah's house.

**C3. The text names that father.**
- [L1] Luke 2:48 gives Mary's own words: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L3] The narrator says "the parents brought in the child Jesus" (Luke 2:27), "his parents went to Jerusalem" (Luke 2:41), and "Joseph and his mother marvelled" (Luke 2:33).
- [L3] The town says "Is not this Joseph's son?" (Luke 4:22) and "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" (John 6:42). A disciple says "Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph" (John 1:45).
- [L3] Joseph is "of the house of David" (Luke 1:27) and "of the house and lineage of David" (Luke 2:4). The angel says "Joseph, thou son of David" (Matthew 1:20).
- [L2] *ho patēr sou* (G3962) means "thy father," in direct speech. *goneis* (G1118) means parents, and the narrator uses it in his own voice.

[L4] Mary, the narrator, the town and a disciple name one father [L1, L3]. The one man the rows set in David's house is Joseph [L3]. So the seed of C1 and the father's house of C2 meet in Joseph.

**C4. The means of begetting the canon states is the husband knowing his wife, and Joseph and Mary were husband and wife from the espousal.**
- [L1] Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived."
- [L3] Matthew 1:19 calls him "Joseph her husband."
- [L3] Matthew 1:20, quoted whole: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The margin at "conceived" reads "Gr. begotten."
- [L3] The law calls a betrothed damsel "his neighbour's wife" (Deuteronomy 22:24), betrothed "unto an husband" (Deuteronomy 22:23).
- [L2] *anēr* (G435), husband, at Matthew 1:19. *gynē* (G1135), wife, at Matthew 1:20.

[L4] The seed comes out of a man's loins (C1). The begetting the canon names is the husband knowing his wife [L1]. The rows call Joseph "her husband" and Mary "thy wife" from the espousal [L3, L2]. So Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal, and the child is of his loins.

---

## Against the defender's links

### LINK D1: "before they came together" and Joseph's intent

The defender writes that *synerchomai* means "to come together as a married couple." Matthew sets the meaning of the phrase by the step that follows it.
- [L1] Matthew 1:24: "and took unto him his wife."
- [L3] The law names the same step for a betrothed man. Deuteronomy 20:7: "what man [is there] that hath betrothed a wife, and hath not taken her?"

[L4] Matthew's order runs from the finding (1:18) to the taking (1:24) [L1]. The law names the taking as the step after betrothal [L3]. So "before they came together" dates the finding before she came into his house. It fits my link, because C4 places the union inside the espousal, and the espousal comes before the taking.

On Matthew 1:19, the verse states intent and two grounds: *dikaios ōn*, being just, and *mē thelōn autēn paradeigmatisai*, unwilling to make her a public example. The verb of the intent is *eboulēthē*, he was minded. No verb of knowing stands in the verse.

On the source the angel names in 1:20, *ek* (G1537) with God or the Spirit marks covenant origin in its New Testament rows. John 1:13 reads "born... of God." 1 John 5:1 reads "is born of God." The margin there is "Gr. has been born," and it is the same verb, *gennaō* (G1080), said of believers who have fathers in the flesh. The row that carries "of the Holy Ghost" also names "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife." It fits my link: the angel grounds the command to take her in the child's covenant origin, while the father of the house is addressed by his Davidic name.

### LINK D2: "I know not a man" and "knew her not till"

- [L1] Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" The words are *andra ou ginōskō*, in the present indicative, her state when the angel spoke.
- [L3] Luke 1:31 puts the conception in the future: "behold, thou shalt conceive in thy womb." The verb is *syllēmpsē*, future, "thou shalt conceive."

[L4] At Luke 1:34 the conception is still future [L3]. Mary's present state is the state before the conception [L1, L2]. So Luke 1:34 dates her state at the announcement. It fits my link, which places the union after the announcement and within the espousal.

- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L3] Matthew 1:24 comes first: "took unto him his wife."
- [L2] *ouk eginōsken autēn heōs hou eteken* means "he was not knowing her until she brought forth." The imperfect runs from the taking to the birth.

[L4] The abstinence follows the taking [L3]. The taking follows the finding of the child (Matthew 1:18) [L1]. So Matthew 1:25 covers the pregnancy after the taking. It fits my link: the conception came before the finding, inside the espousal, and the abstinence was bounded to the pregnancy by "till."

The defender's own [L3], Genesis 4:1 ("Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived"), is my C4 footing. It names knowing as the means of conception. The timing rows date when that knowing did and did not take place.

### LINK D3: Luke 1:35's verbs and "therefore"

- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee."
- [L2] *eperchomai* (G1904) means to come upon. *episkiazō* (G1982) means to overshadow; it occurs in 5 verses (Matthew 17:5; Mark 9:7; Luke 1:35; Luke 9:34; Acts 5:15).
